approach: saddleback search with value-space binary search and query caching
details: Read n and k from stdin. If n equals 1, query a[1][1] and output DONE with that value. Otherwise maintain a query cache (a std::unordered_map keyed by (i,j) packed as a long long, or a 2D vector of optional or sentinel-marked entries). Define query(i,j) that returns the cached value or else writes QUERY i j to stdout, flushes, reads the response integer, caches it, and returns it. Define countLE(v) using saddleback search: start at i=1, j=n with cnt=0; while i is at most n and j is at least 1, fetch x = query(i,j); if x is at most v then cnt += j and i++ else j--; return cnt (this counts entries that are at most v in roughly 2n-1 cached steps). Query a[1][1] as lo and a[n][n] as hi. Binary search integer v in [lo, hi] to find the smallest v such that countLE(v) is at least k: while lo is less than hi, mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, if countLE(mid) is at least k then hi = mid else lo = mid + 1; after the loop the answer is lo. Output a single line DONE followed by a space and the integer lo, then flush. Edge cases: n equals 1 (just output a[1][1]); k equals 1 (answer is a[1][1]); k equals n times n (answer is a[n][n]); use long long for all values since matrix entries can be up to 10 to the 18; always flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE.
rationale: Saddleback search counts entries at most v in O(n) cached queries and value-space binary search converges in roughly 60 iterations, with the cache reusing the heavily overlapping staircase paths; this is a clean baseline that opens a new direction and gives us a first score to refine against.

approach: diagonal precomputation with bracketed saddleback binary search
details: Build on the current saddleback solution. Add a preprocessing step before the main binary search: query a[i][i] for i from 1 to n inclusive, storing each via the existing cache. Then derive tighter initial bounds from monotonicity. Find i_hi as the smallest i in [1, n] with i*i at least k and set hi = a[i_hi][i_hi] (if no such i, keep hi = a[n][n]). Find i_lo as the largest i in [1, n] with (n-i+1)*(n-i+1) at least n*n - k + 1 and set lo = a[i_lo][i_lo] (if no such i, keep lo = a[1][1]). These bounds are valid because the top-left i by i block has i*i cells all at most a[i][i], so countLE(a[i][i]) is at least i*i (hence ans is at most a[i][i] when i*i at least k); and the bottom-right (n-i+1) by (n-i+1) block has (n-i+1)*(n-i+1) cells all at least a[i][i], so countGE(a[i][i]) is at least (n-i+1)*(n-i+1), giving ans at least a[i][i] when (n-i+1)*(n-i+1) at least n*n - k + 1. Then run the existing saddleback value-space binary search on [lo, hi]; the existing cache lets diagonal cells be reused by any saddleback path that revisits them. Edge cases: if lo equals hi after bracketing, output DONE lo immediately and exit; keep the existing n equals 1 fast path and the k equals 1 / k equals n*n fast paths; before the new diagonal sweep, still query a[1][1] and a[n][n] first so the original bounds remain valid fallbacks; iterate the diagonal loop only when n is at least 2; use long long for all values and indices since matrix entries reach 10 to the 18.
rationale: The diagonal supplies n cached anchor values that compress the binary search range using simple monotonicity bounds, shrinking the 60-iteration value-space sweep into far fewer effective iterations while seeding the cache; this refines the still-maturing saddleback direction.

approach: diagonal-indexed binary search with bracketed refinement
details: Build on the current solution. Replace the algebraic i times i bracket with a direct binary search over diagonal indices using countLE. After the existing diagonal precomputation populates diag[1..n] (a sorted non-decreasing sequence since the matrix is monotone along the main diagonal), perform a binary search on indices to find the smallest index i in [1, n] with countLE(diag[i]) at least k. Use lo_i = 1, hi_i = n; while lo_i is less than hi_i, mid_i = (lo_i + hi_i) / 2, if countLE(diag[mid_i]) at least k then hi_i = mid_i else lo_i = mid_i + 1. After the loop, the answer is at most diag[lo_i]. Then set vlo = (lo_i greater than 1 then diag[lo_i - 1] + 1 else a[1][1]) and vhi = diag[lo_i]. If vlo greater than or equal to vhi, output DONE followed by vhi and exit. Otherwise do integer value-space binary search on [vlo, vhi] using the existing saddleback with the cache already heavily populated by the diagonal queries and the index binary search: while vlo less than vhi, mid = vlo + (vhi - vlo) / 2, if countLE(mid) at least k then vhi = mid else vlo = mid + 1; output DONE followed by vlo. Remove the old algebraic i_lo and i_hi bracketing code entirely (the new diag-index binary search replaces it). Keep the n equals 1, k equals 1, k equals n times n fast paths and keep the unordered_map cache. Edge cases: if countLE(diag[1]) is already at least k then lo_i becomes 1 and vlo equals a[1][1] which is the correct lower bound; if multiple diag values are equal in a region the bracket collapses naturally to a single value; use long long for all values and counts; flush after every QUERY and after DONE.
rationale: Binary searching diagonal indices via countLE tightens the bracket to two adjacent diagonal values (a much smaller integer gap than the algebraic i times i bounds), so the subsequent integer binary search converges in far fewer iterations and the cache from diagonal queries seeds the saddleback paths densely; this continues the still-maturing diagonal direction.

approach: cached-value-guided binary search with countLE early termination
details: Revert to commit e4dcd04 (the iteration 1 saddleback plus diagonal precomputation plus algebraic bracket). Keep the diagonal precomputation, the algebraic i-squared bracket using i_hi and i_lo, the n equals 1 fast path, and the k equals 1 / k equals n times n fast paths unchanged. Make two changes to the integer value-space binary search and to countLE.; Change 1 (cached-value-guided midpoints): maintain a std::set of long long named cachedVals that is updated inside the query function every time a new value is inserted into the existing unordered_map cache (call cachedVals.insert(v) right after the unordered_map insert). At each binary search step, use cachedVals.upper_bound(vlo) and cachedVals.upper_bound(vhi) to locate the iterator range of cached values that are strictly greater than vlo and at most vhi; if the range size is at least one, advance the begin iterator by half the range size and use that value as the binary search midpoint v; otherwise fall back to the integer midpoint v = vlo + (vhi - vlo) / 2. Then compute countLE(v) and update vlo or vhi using the standard rule (count at least k means vhi = v, else vlo = v + 1).; Change 2 (countLE early termination): inside the saddleback while loop in countLE, immediately after the cnt += j increment (i.e. after each downward step), check if cnt is at least k and if so return cnt early. Also at the top of each loop iteration compute maxFuture = (long long)(n - i + 1) times j (an upper bound on the remaining cells the walk could still contribute if every future visited cell turned out to be at most v) and if cnt + maxFuture is strictly less than k return cnt early. These two early exits do not change correctness because the value-space binary search caller branches only on whether the returned count is at least k.; Edge cases: do the std::set update only when the unordered_map insert actually adds a new key so cachedVals stays consistent; handle cachedVals.empty() and empty-range cases by falling back to integer midpoint; pass k by capturing the global variable (no signature change) and keep returning long long; use long long for cnt, maxFuture, and v throughout since matrix values reach 10 to the 18; flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE.
rationale: Iteration 1 is the still-maturing best at 29.37 while iteration 2 regressed to 17.83 because each diagonal-index BS step added a full countLE traversal; cached-value midpoints converge faster because the true k-th value is one of the matrix cell values already present in the cache after the diagonal and prior saddlebacks, and countLE early termination cuts queries per call whenever the walk can decide at least k or less than k before reaching the corner, so both changes refine the saddleback direction without adding the extra countLE calls that hurt iteration 2.

approach: row pointer countLE with bracketed per-row binary search
details: Revert to commit e4dcd04 (the iteration 1 solution: diagonal precomputation, algebraic i-squared bracket, saddleback BS, cache). Keep the diagonal precomputation querying a[i][i] for i in 1..n, the algebraic i_lo and i_hi bracket logic, the unordered_map cache plus query helper, and all fast paths (n equals 1, k equals 1, k equals n times n). Replace the saddleback countLE and the integer value-space binary search with a row-pointer per-row binary search countLE that maintains persistent per-row bracket pointers across all binary search iterations.; Add two arrays sized n+2: rowLowJ initialized to 0 for every i and rowHighJ initialized to n+1 for every i. Invariants throughout the whole BS: for each i in 1..n, a[i][rowLowJ[i]] is at most lo using the sentinel that a[i][0] is treated as negative infinity (never actually queried); a[i][rowHighJ[i]] is strictly greater than hi using the sentinel that a[i][n+1] is treated as positive infinity (never actually queried).; New countLE(v) returns long long and writes per-row results into a vector<int> rowJ of size n+2. Body: long long cnt = 0; for i from 1 to n: int loJ = rowLowJ[i], hiJ = rowHighJ[i]; while loJ + 1 is less than hiJ: int midJ = (loJ + hiJ) / 2; long long x = query(i, midJ); if x is at most v then loJ = midJ else hiJ = midJ; rowJ[i] = loJ; cnt += loJ; return cnt.; New main BS loop replacing the previous integer BS: while lo is less than hi: long long mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; long long c = countLE(mid); if c is at least k then hi = mid and for each i from 1 to n set rowHighJ[i] = min(rowHighJ[i], rowJ[i] + 1); else lo = mid + 1 and for each i from 1 to n set rowLowJ[i] = max(rowLowJ[i], rowJ[i]). After the loop output DONE followed by a space and lo and flush.; Correctness notes: the rowLowJ update is safe because a[i][rowJ[i]] is at most mid which is at most new lo; the rowHighJ update is safe because a[i][rowJ[i] + 1] is strictly greater than mid equals new hi (per-row BS guarantees this whenever rowJ[i] + 1 is at most n; when rowJ[i] equals n the value rowJ[i] + 1 equals n + 1 which is the positive-infinity sentinel).; Edge cases: never query column 0 or column n + 1 (the BS while-condition loJ + 1 less than hiJ keeps midJ in [1, n] whenever loJ is at least 0 and hiJ is at most n + 1); if rowLowJ[i] + 1 equals rowHighJ[i] the inner while skips and rowJ[i] equals rowLowJ[i] with zero queries for that row; keep the diagonal precomputation so the per-row BS often hits a cached a[i][i]; allocate rowJ once outside the BS loop and reuse it; use long long for all values, k, cnt, mid, lo, hi; flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE. Do not call the old saddleback anywhere.
rationale: Saddleback countLE costs roughly 2n queries per call and repeats for each of about log V binary search iterations re-traversing mostly the same staircase; replacing it with per-row binary search that persists rowLowJ and rowHighJ pointers across iterations amortizes total query cost toward O(n log n) since each row pointer pair shrinks monotonically toward a single column, opening a new direction distinct from the maturing saddleback path.

approach: sparse algebraic diagonal anchors with on-demand corner queries
details: Revert to commit e4dcd04 (iteration 1 saddleback plus full diagonal precomputation plus algebraic i-squared bracket). Keep the n equals 1 fast path, the k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, the unordered_map cache and query helper, the saddleback countLE and the integer value-space binary search exactly as they are; the only change is removing the upfront full diagonal sweep and querying only the two diagonal anchor cells that actually feed the algebraic bracket. Concretely: delete the block that allocates vector<long long> diag of size n+1 and the loop that runs from i equals 2 to i equals n-1 setting diag[i] equals query(i, i). Keep the existing loop that finds i_hi as the smallest i in [1, n] with i times i at least k and the existing loop that finds i_lo as the largest i in [1, n] with (n - i + 1) times (n - i + 1) at least n times n - k + 1 (these loops are pure arithmetic and do no queries). After i_hi is found, if it is valid then set hi to query(i_hi, i_hi); after i_lo is found, if it is valid then set lo to query(i_lo, i_lo). When i_hi is 1 or n or i_lo is 1 or n the query function will hit the cache from the earlier a[1][1] and a[n][n] queries so no extra QUERY is sent in those cases. Drop the local diag array entirely (it is no longer referenced). Everything downstream — the lo equals hi early DONE, the integer value-space binary search loop, the saddleback countLE — stays identical to e4dcd04. Remove the row-pointer machinery from the current iteration 4 solution (rowLowJ, rowHighJ, rowJ, the per-row inner BS); the new countLE is the original e4dcd04 saddleback walk from (1, n) toward (n, 1). Edge cases: when i_hi is undefined keep hi at a[n][n]; when i_lo is undefined keep lo at a[1][1]; when both anchors coincide and the immediate lo equals hi check fires, output DONE lo and exit; use long long for all values, lo, hi, mid and counts since matrix entries reach 10 to the 18; flush after every QUERY and after DONE.
rationale: Full diagonal sweep on iteration 1 cost n queries but only two of them (a[i_hi][i_hi] and a[i_lo][i_lo]) actually fed the algebraic bracket, and any saddleback walk gains at most one diagonal cache hit per call because monotone staircase paths visit at most one cell where i equals j, so dropping the n minus 2 unused diagonal queries returns nearly n queries to the BS budget while preserving identical bracket tightness; this continues the still-maturing saddleback direction.

approach: saddleback countLE with cumulative early termination
details: Build on the current iteration 5 solution (b105bf6). Keep everything identical except countLE: keep the n equals 1 fast path, the k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, the unordered_map cache plus query helper, the a[1][1] and a[n][n] initial queries, the algebraic i_hi and i_lo loops, the on-demand query(i_hi, i_hi) and query(i_lo, i_lo) anchor fetches, the lo equals hi early DONE check, and the integer value-space binary search loop with its mid update rule. Modify only the saddleback function long long countLE(long long v). The current body walks from i equals 1, j equals n, while i is at most n and j is at least 1, fetches x equals query(i, j), and either does cnt plus equals j and i plus plus when x is at most v else does j minus minus, then returns cnt. Insert two safe early termination checks at the very top of each loop iteration, before fetching x. Check one: if cnt is at least k, return cnt immediately (cnt can only grow so the caller comparison cnt at least k still holds). Check two: compute long long upperBound equal to cnt plus (long long)(n minus i plus 1) times j; if upperBound is strictly less than k, return cnt (this is the maximum extra cells the remaining walk could possibly contribute, since at most (n minus i plus 1) rows remain and within each row at most j columns lie at or before column j; if even that maximum cannot reach k, the true count stays strictly less than k). Use the (long long) cast before multiplying so the product does not overflow int. Reference the existing global long long k inside countLE (no signature change). Do not modify the saddleback step otherwise (no cached-value midpoint logic, no extra data structures, no preprocessing change). Edge cases: the existing while condition i is at most n and j is at least 1 already prevents underflow; when i has reached n plus 1 or j has reached 0 the upper bound becomes cnt and the loop would exit naturally on the next iteration anyway so correctness is preserved; the early returns must use long long arithmetic to avoid 32 bit overflow for n equals 2000; flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE as before.
rationale: When mid is far from the true k-th value (most binary search iterations early on), either countLE rapidly exceeds k from the first few row contributions and check one triggers, or the upper bound on remaining cells falls below k well before the saddleback reaches the corner and check two triggers; both shortcuts cut queries per countLE call without changing the cnt at least k branch the caller relies on, refining the still-maturing sparse-anchor saddleback direction toward its query-count ceiling.

details: Build on the current iteration 6 solution (7117b63). Keep the n equals 1 fast path, the k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, the unordered_map cache plus query helper, the initial a[1][1] and a[n][n] queries, the lo equals hi early DONE check, the integer value-space binary search loop, and the saddleback countLE with the two early termination checks all unchanged. Replace the existing single-point i_hi and i_lo algebraic anchor queries with a hyperbola sweep that queries multiple algebraic anchor cells along the i times j equals k boundary (for hi) and the bottom-right boundary (n minus i plus 1) times (n minus j plus 1) equals n times n minus k plus 1 (for lo), taking the running min for hi and the running max for lo.; Concretely, delete the existing i_hi loop and the if (i_hi not equal to minus 1) hi equals query(i_hi, i_hi) line, and delete the existing i_lo loop and the if (i_lo not equal to minus 1) lo equals query(i_lo, i_lo) line. In their place insert the two passes below, before the lo equals hi early DONE check.; Pass A (tighten hi): for each long long i in the fixed list 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, n (powers of two from 1 up to 2048 together with n itself), if i is in [1, n] compute long long jH equals (k plus i minus 1) divided by i (integer ceiling of k divided by i using long long arithmetic); if jH is in [1, n] then call long long v equals query((int)i, (int)jH) and set hi equals min(hi, v). This is valid because i times jH is at least k, so the top-left i by jH rectangle contains at least k cells all at most a[i][jH], hence countLE(a[i][jH]) is at least k and the k-th smallest is at most a[i][jH].; Pass B (tighten lo): for each long long i in the same list, if i is in [1, n] compute long long m equals (long long)n minus i plus 1, long long target equals (long long)n times n minus k plus 1, long long p equals (target plus m minus 1) divided by m (integer ceiling); if p is in [1, n] then let long long jL equals (long long)n plus 1 minus p; if jL is in [1, n] then call long long v equals query((int)i, (int)jL) and set lo equals max(lo, v). This is valid because the rectangle rows [i..n] by columns [jL..n] has m times p at least n times n minus k plus 1 cells all at least a[i][jL], so countGE(a[i][jL]) is at least n times n minus k plus 1, hence at most k minus 1 cells are strictly less than a[i][jL], so a[i][jL] is at most the k-th smallest.; Edge cases: skip any anchor whose jH or jL falls outside [1, n]; use long long throughout for k, n times n, m, target, p, jH, jL so no overflow occurs when n is 2000 and k can be up to 4 million; the unordered_map cache deduplicates anchor cells that coincide with each other or with a[1][1] or a[n][n] so no extra QUERY is sent in those cases; do not change countLE, the saddleback walk, or the integer BS loop; flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE.
rationale: The current diagonal anchor (i_hi, i_hi) is just one point on the i times j equals k curve while many other points on the same curve can yield strictly tighter upper bounds because a[i][jH] for jH less than i_hi is at most a[i_hi][i_hi]; sweeping a sparse logarithmic set of anchor points and taking the running min for hi (and the running max for lo via the symmetric bottom-right curve) often tightens the integer BS range by orders of magnitude at the cost of about 22 extra anchor queries, and the cached anchor cells also seed subsequent saddleback walks; this refines the still-maturing sparse-anchor saddleback direction toward a lower query count.

approach: column 1 and column n sparse anchor preprocessing with row range skip in countLE
details: Revert to commit 7117b63 (iteration 6: sparse anchor saddleback with countLE early termination). Keep the n equals 1 fast path, the k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, the unordered_map cache plus query helper, the initial a[1][1] and a[n][n] queries, the on-demand i_hi and i_lo diagonal anchor logic, the lo equals hi early DONE check, the integer value-space binary search, and the saddleback countLE with the two early termination checks. Add a column 1 and column n anchor preprocessing pass plus a row range skip optimization inside countLE.; Anchor preprocessing (placed after the i_hi and i_lo on-demand anchor queries and before the lo equals hi check): define const long long iList equals 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, (long long)n. Allocate two file-scope vectors of pair<int, long long>: col1Vals and colNVals. For each i in iList that is in [1, n], call query((int)i, 1) and push_back (i, returned value) into col1Vals, then call query((int)i, n) and push_back (i, returned value) into colNVals (skip duplicates by using a small set of already-added i values so n and 1 are not added twice if the list contains them more than once). Sort both vectors by i ascending; by column monotonicity (a[i+1][1] at least a[i][1] and a[i+1][n] at least a[i][n]) the value sequence is also monotone non-decreasing.; Algebraic bracket tightening from the new anchors: for each (i, v) in colNVals, if (long long)i times n is at least k then set hi equals min(hi, v) (the top-left i by n rectangle holds i times n cells all at most v by both monotones). For each (i, v) in col1Vals, if (long long)(i minus 1) times n is strictly less than k then set lo equals max(lo, v) (the bottom-right (n minus i plus 1) by n rectangle holds (n minus i plus 1) times n cells all at least v, hence countLE(v minus 1) is at most (i minus 1) times n, so if (i minus 1) times n is less than k the k-th smallest is at least v).; Row range skip in countLE: at the start of each countLE(v) call, compute iSkipN equals the largest anchor row in colNVals whose stored value is at most v (default 0 if none); compute iSkipZero equals the smallest anchor row in col1Vals whose stored value is strictly greater than v (default n plus 1 if none). Since both vectors are at most 13 entries, a linear scan is fine (scan colNVals descending and break on first value at most v; scan col1Vals ascending and break on first value strictly greater than v). Initialize cnt equals (long long)n times iSkipN; if cnt is at least k return cnt immediately. Set i equals iSkipN plus 1, j equals n, iMax equals iSkipZero minus 1. If i is greater than iMax return cnt immediately. Otherwise run the saddleback walk constrained to rows in [iSkipN plus 1, iMax]: while i is at most iMax and j is at least 1: existing early termination check 1 (if cnt is at least k return cnt); replace the n minus i plus 1 in early termination check 2 with iMax minus i plus 1 so it reads if cnt + (long long)(iMax minus i plus 1) times j is strictly less than k return cnt; query x at (i, j); if x is at most v then cnt plus equals j and i plus plus else j minus minus. Return cnt.; Correctness: column monotonicity guarantees rows 1..iSkipN all have a[i][n] at most a[iSkipN][n] at most v, hence (by row monotonicity) every cell in those rows is at most v contributing n each; column monotonicity guarantees rows iSkipZero..n all have a[i][1] at least a[iSkipZero][1] strictly greater than v, hence every cell in those rows exceeds v contributing 0 each; the saddleback only walks the uncertain band (iSkipN, iMax]. The early termination upper bound is iMax minus i plus 1 rather than n minus i plus 1 because rows beyond iMax contribute 0.; Edge cases: i equals 1 in iList causes query (1, 1) which hits the cache from the existing a[1][1] query (no extra QUERY); i equals n causes query (n, n) which hits the cache from the existing a[n][n] query; if iSkipN equals n the entire matrix is at most v and cnt equals (long long)n times n at least k so we return immediately; if no anchor triggers either skip the countLE collapses to the original iteration 6 saddleback behavior since iSkipN equals 0 and iMax equals n; allocate col1Vals and colNVals once outside the BS loop and reuse them; use long long for cnt, k, all products, and all values throughout since matrix entries reach 10 to the 18; flush after every QUERY and after DONE; never query column 0 or column n plus 1.
rationale: The current sparse-anchor saddleback hits its query budget primarily inside the saddleback walk at roughly 2n cells per countLE call; column 1 and column n sparse anchors let the saddleback skip whole row ranges that are wholly at most v (contributing n by row monotonicity) or wholly greater than v (contributing 0) using only column monotonicity, slashing per-call queries when v is near a value extreme (common in early BS iterations); the new anchors also contribute complementary algebraic tightening via i times n and (i minus 1) times n bounds that the existing diagonal i_hi and i_lo anchors do not capture, refining the still-maturing sparse-anchor saddleback direction by attacking the per-countLE cost rather than the BS iteration count.

approach: row 1 and row n sparse anchor preprocessing with column range skip in countLE
details: Build on the current iteration 8 solution (e3cb5bb). Keep the n equals 1 fast path, the k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, the unordered_map cache plus query helper, the initial a[1][1] and a[n][n] queries, the on-demand i_hi and i_lo diagonal anchor logic, the col1Vals and colNVals preprocessing, the existing algebraic tightening from col anchors, the lo equals hi early DONE check, and the integer value-space binary search loop. Add symmetric row 1 and row n sparse anchor preprocessing plus column range skip inside countLE.; Anchor preprocessing (placed immediately after the existing col1Vals and colNVals loop and sorts): define the same jList of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, (long long)n. Allocate two file-scope vectors of pair<int, long long>: row1Vals and rowNVals. For each j in jList that is in [1, n], call query(1, (int)j) and push_back (j, returned value) into row1Vals, then call query(n, (int)j) and push_back (j, returned value) into rowNVals (use a small set of already-added j values to skip duplicates so n and 1 are not added twice when jList contains them). Sort both vectors by j ascending; by row monotonicity (a[1][j plus 1] at least a[1][j] and a[n][j plus 1] at least a[n][j]) the value sequences are non-decreasing.; Algebraic bracket tightening from the new anchors (placed right after the existing col-anchor algebraic tightening loops): for each (j, v) in rowNVals, if (long long)j times n is at least k then set hi equals min(hi, v) (the n by j top-left rectangle holds j times n cells all at most v since a[i,j-prime] is at most a[n][j-prime] is at most a[n][j] equals v for i in [1,n] and j-prime in [1,j]). For each (j, v) in row1Vals, if (long long)(j minus 1) times n is strictly less than k then set lo equals max(lo, v) (cells in cols j..n satisfy a[i,j-prime] at least a[1][j-prime] at least a[1][j] equals v, contributing (n minus j plus 1) times n cells that are at least v, so countLT(v) is at most (j minus 1) times n; since this is less than k the k-th smallest is at least v).; Column range skip in countLE: extend the existing iSkipN and iSkipZero scans with two more scans. Compute jSkipN equals the largest anchor col in rowNVals whose stored value is at most v (default 0 if none) by scanning rowNVals descending and breaking on the first value at most v; compute jSkipZero equals the smallest anchor col in row1Vals whose stored value is strictly greater than v (default n plus 1 if none) by scanning row1Vals ascending and breaking on the first value strictly greater than v. Define iLow equals iSkipN, iHigh equals iSkipZero minus 1, jLow equals jSkipN, jHigh equals jSkipZero minus 1. Set long long cnt equals (long long)iLow times n plus (long long)(n minus iLow) times jLow (rows 1..iLow wholly at most v give iLow times n cells; cols 1..jLow wholly at most v in remaining rows iLow plus 1..n give (n minus iLow) times jLow cells; this is consistent because jLow greater than 0 forces iSkipZero equal to n plus 1 hence iHigh equal to n via the contradiction a[n][1] greater than v versus a[n][jLow] at most v under column monotonicity). If cnt is at least k return cnt. If iLow plus 1 is greater than iHigh or jLow plus 1 is greater than jHigh return cnt. Otherwise saddleback inside the uncertain box: set int i equals iLow plus 1, int j equals jHigh; while i is at most iHigh and j is greater than jLow: if cnt is at least k return cnt; long long upperBound equals cnt plus (long long)(iHigh minus i plus 1) times (j minus jLow); if upperBound is strictly less than k return cnt; long long x equals query(i, j); if x is at most v then cnt plus equals (j minus jLow) and i plus plus else j minus minus. approach: lazy lo and hi bracket tightening on every cached query

(b) The bottom-right (n minus i plus 1) by (n minus j plus 1) rectangle contains m cells all at least v, so countLT(v) is at most n times n minus m, hence if m is at least n times n minus k plus 1 then countLT(v) is at most k minus 1 so the answer is at least v, giving a valid lo candidate. approach: cached matrix value midpoint pivot in value space binary search

Initialize two candidates: long long candA equals LLONG_MAX and long long candB equals LLONG_MAX. If it is not cachedSet.end() and the dereferenced value is at least lo and strictly less than hi then set candA equal to that dereferenced value. If it is not cachedSet.begin() then let auto itP equal std::prev(it) and if the dereferenced itP is at least lo and strictly less than hi then set candB equal to that dereferenced value. If both candA and candB are LLONG_MAX set mid to imid; else if only candA is valid set mid to candA; else if only candB is valid set mid to candB; else pick the candidate closer to imid by setting mid to candB if imid minus candB is strictly less than candA minus imid else setting mid to candA. The resulting mid is always in the closed-open interval from lo to hi minus 1 inclusive which guarantees BS progress: either countLE(mid) is at least k and hi equals min(hi, mid) shrinks the upper end strictly, or countLE(mid) is strictly less than k and lo equals max(lo, mid plus 1) shrinks the lower end strictly.; Edge cases: include climits for LLONG_MAX (already pulled in by bits/stdc++.h on standard distros, otherwise add an explicit include); cachedSet.insert is amortized O(log n_set) per call which is negligible relative to the QUERY round-trip cost; cachedSet.lower_bound is O(log n_set); std::prev requires the iterator not equal cachedSet.begin which is explicitly checked; never pick a cached value equal to hi because that would not make BS progress (the strict less than hi guard on both candA and candB prevents it); the lazy hi tightening inside query may shrink hi to a value equal to the freshly cached v during a saddleback walk, but the next outer BS midpoint selection naturally excludes that value because of the strict less than hi check; use long long for imid, mid, candA, candB and all matrix values since entries reach 10 to the 18; flush after every QUERY and after the final DONE; the lo equals hi early termination guard at the top of the BS while loop already short-circuits any degenerate range.
rationale: Current solution still does roughly log V value-space BS iterations after algebraic bracket tightening and most of those midpoints test integer values that do not exist anywhere in the matrix at all so countLE(mid) returns the same count as countLE(nearest_cached_value) yet costs a full saddleback walk; the true k-th smallest must equal some a[i][j] and the cache already contains thousands of real matrix values after the first few saddleback walks and anchor preprocessing, so snapping each midpoint to the cached matrix value closest to the integer midpoint converges the BS to the answer in roughly log (number of cached values in the current bracket) iterations instead of log V iterations without changing per-call query cost or correctness, refining the still maturing sparse-anchor saddleback direction by attacking the BS iteration count instead of the per-call cost.

approach: small-k min heap and large-k max heap dispatch with saddleback fallback
details: Revert to commit 3d2dc51 (iteration 10 lazy lo and hi tightening on sparse row and col anchor saddleback). Keep n equals 1 fast path, k equals 1 and k equals n times n fast paths, unordered_map cache and query helper, initial a[1][1] and a[n][n] queries, on-demand i_hi and i_lo diagonal anchor logic, col1Vals colNVals row1Vals rowNVals sparse anchor preprocessing and their algebraic tightening loops, lo equals hi early DONE check, integer value-space binary search loop, saddleback countLE with row range skip column range skip and the two cumulative early termination checks, and the lazy in-query lo and hi bracket tightening inside the query helper. Call long long v00 equals query(1, 1) (a cache hit), push the tuple (v00, 1, 1), set visited[1][1] to 1. Loop long long r from 1 to k inclusive: extract the top either via structured bindings auto [v, i, j] equals pqMin.top() or via std::get<0>, std::get<1>, std::get<2>, then call pqMin.pop(). If r equals k then write DONE followed by a space then v to stdout, call cout.flush(), and return 0. Otherwise if i plus 1 is at most n and visited[i plus 1][j] equals 0 then long long vd equals query(i plus 1, j), set visited[i plus 1][j] to 1, push the tuple (vd, i plus 1, j); and if j plus 1 is at most n and visited[i][j plus 1] equals 0 then long long vr equals query(i, j plus 1), set visited[i][j plus 1] to 1, push the tuple (vr, i, j plus 1). ; Large-k branch: else if targetLarge is at most T, allocate the same visited array. Declare std::priority_queue<std::tuple<long long, int, int>> pqMax which uses the default less ordering and is therefore a max heap. Call long long vNN equals query(n, n) (a cache hit), push the tuple (vNN, n, n), set visited[n][n] to 1. Loop long long r from 1 to targetLarge inclusive: extract the top auto [v, i, j] equals pqMax.top() then pqMax.pop(). If r equals targetLarge then write DONE followed by a space then v to stdout, call cout.flush(), and return 0. Otherwise if i minus 1 is at least 1 and visited[i minus 1][j] equals 0 then long long vu equals query(i minus 1, j), set visited[i minus 1][j] to 1, push the tuple (vu, i minus 1, j); and if j minus 1 is at least 1 and visited[i][j minus 1] equals 0 then long long vl equals query(i, j minus 1), set visited[i][j minus 1] to 1, push the tuple (vl, i, j minus 1). ; Else (when k is strictly greater than T and targetLarge is strictly greater than T) fall through to the existing anchor preprocessing and value-space BS exactly as in 3d2dc51 without modification. ; Correctness: in a row and column sorted matrix the global minimum sits at (1, 1) and after popping any cell (i, j) the next-smallest unpopped cell is either (i plus 1, j-prime) or (i-prime, j plus 1) for some prior popped (i-prime, j-prime), since every unpopped cell has at least one popped predecessor along the down-or-right partial order; pushing (i plus 1, j) and (i, j plus 1) when (i, j) is popped therefore keeps the heap a superset of all candidates for the next pop, so after k pops the popped value is the k-th smallest.
